topics.title: The make-up department of Gemini Studios
topics.ncert_sections: Opening section: Pancake, the make-up room and its staff

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Pancake make-up, the make-up room and the 'fiery misery' of those being made up.
Explain how the mixed staff of the make-up department illustrates national integration.
Interpret the strict hierarchy of the make-up department and the author's ironic view of it.

topics.title: The office boy and the author's work
topics.ncert_sections: The office boy, the author's cubicle and the office boy's frustration

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why the office boy joined the studio, why he was frustrated and whom he blamed.
Describe the author's job at Gemini Studios and why others thought he did nothing.
Identify Subbu's many talents as film-maker, poet, novelist and actor.
Describe Subbu's loyalty, generosity and the reasons he had enemies.

topics.title: The Story Department and the legal adviser
topics.ncert_sections: The Story Department, the lawyer and the actress

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the legal adviser unwittingly ended an actress's career.
Interpret the lawyer's isolation among the poets and the irony of his losing his job.

topics.title: Communism and the Moral Re-Armament visit
topics.ncert_sections: The poets' politics and the MRA visit of 1952

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the Gemini poets' notions about Communism and their political outlook.
Explain the MRA's visit, its plays and their influence on Tamil drama.

topics.title: Stephen Spender's visit and the mystery solved
topics.ncert_sections: The English poet's visit, The Encounter and The God That Failed

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the English poet's visit and why it baffled the Gemini staff.
Explain how the author identified Spender and why the visit stopped being a mystery.

topics.title: Humour, style and vocabulary
topics.ncert_sections: Gentle humour, rambling style and words and expressions from the text

concepts.learning_objective: Infer the meaning of expressions such as 'blew over' and 'the favourite haunt' from context.
Analyse how the author uses gentle irony and self-mockery to point out human foibles.
